citation: Jung W et al. 2026. Spatial transcriptome mapping identifies Ppara-Anxa2 cross-talk in microplastic-induced hepatotoxicity. Sci Adv 12(25):eaec8681
access_level: Full text + all 18 supplementary tables parsed
category: PE x MASH diet; source of our dataset
scientific_question: Does oral PE cause hepatotoxicity and worsen diet-induced MASH, and which spatial/cellular mechanism (PPARa-Anxa2 in pericentral hepatocytes) mediates it?
design_and_n: 2x2 diet (CD/MD) x gavage (vehicle/PE), 8 wk. Phenotype n=5/group (Table S1). Bulk RNA-seq n=4/5/5/5 (GEO; not stated in paper). Xenium 19 samples on 2 slides. ChIP-qPCR n=5/group. In vitro n=3.
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse C57BL/6 (Jackson), male, 8 wk at start
exposure_polymer_size_dose_route_duratio: PE 10-150 um (Cospheric), 2 mg/mouse/day, oral gavage in 0.1% Tween-20, 8 wk; no size/zeta/endotoxin characterisation
diet_or_second_factor: Research Diets D09100304 (CD) vs D09100310 (40% fat, 20% fructose, 2% cholesterol)
datasets_generated_and_reused: Generated GSE294180 (bulk counts), Zenodo 19603085 (Xenium). Re-used GSE245069 (Li 2025, fig. S2F-G), GSE282998, GSE8295 (Ppara-null), ChIP-seq SRX5142528/SRX5028180
statistical_or_ml_models: fastp-Salmon-tximport-DESeq2, all 6 pairwise contrasts, |log2FC|>=0.38 & FDR<0.05; fgsea; WGCNA (Ppara hub of MD+PE module); Seurat/SCTransform/Harmony; cell-level FindMarkers + sample pseudobulk DESeq2; betareg and glmmTMB beta GLMM with (1|sample) for proportions; one-way ANOVA+Tukey for phenotypes/qPCR; DESeq2 interaction table (S7) computed but not reported
why_model_fits_or_not: 2x2 question needs an interaction contrast; narrative instead uses pairwise contrasts and set subtraction (more MD DEGs partly because diet effects are large = power difference). Mixed models for spatial proportions are appropriate (avoid pseudoreplication). Ppara headline compares vs CD+Veh, mixing diet and PE.
inputs_features_outputs_targets: Bulk gene counts -> DEG lists, GSEA, WGCNA modules; Xenium cell x gene -> cell types, zonation, proportions; target = PE-responsive genes/cell states; phenotypes ALT, TG, NAS
how_evaluated: FDR/FC thresholds; pseudobulk-bulk Pearson concordance (Fig. 4A, value not given); no external replication of bulk signature
validation_type: Internal + orthogonal: qPCR (Anxa2, fig. S6B), ChIP-qPCR (Fig. 6H, no IgG/input described), in vitro antagonist/siRNA (Fig. 6M-N, no PE-alone arm), external Ppara-null microarray (no PE). No in vivo Ppara loss under PE.
main_findings: ALT up with PE in both diets (Fig. 1E); TG up MD+PE vs MD+Veh (Fig. 1F); lipogenic genes down with PE in both diets (Fasn -1.51/-1.42; Acly, Acaca, Me1, Pnpla3; Fig. 2D, Tables S5/S6); cholesterol synthesis down under CD (Hmgcr -1.38, Sqle -1.45); Ppara +0.53 PE_in_CD (padj 0.011) but +0.34 PE_in_MD (padj 0.23); Anxa2 no bulk PE effect, up spatially in pericentral hepatocytes; midlobular hepatocytes up (Fig. 3D)
actual_limitations: Cage = group; RNA-seq n unstated; synergy from difference-of-significance; S7 interaction list dominated by skeletal-muscle genes (likely carry-over) and not discussed; Harmony across groups may absorb group effects; cell-level DE pseudoreplicated; in vitro arms lack PE-alone reference; ChIP controls not described; Raman only MD slides, no blanks; dose per mouse not per kg; no sample QC reported (our audit: PE libraries shallower)
not_attempted_not_a_flaw: Females; dose-response; time course; non-plastic particle control; in vivo Ppara KO; lipidomics; microbiome; sacrifice time/fasting reporting
interaction_formally_tested_and_reported: Computed (Table S7, 76 genes padj<0.05; Table S12 spatial) but NOT reported or interpreted in text
key_locations: Methods 'Bulk RNA-seq and analysis'; Fig. 1B-F; Fig. 2D-F; Fig. 3D; Fig. 4A,E; Fig. 6C,H,M-N; Tables S1, S5-S7, S12, S18
relevance_to_our_project: Primary dataset. Our factorial re-analysis, split-reference concordance and QC extend it. Discrepancy to resolve: their Ppara PE_in_CD +0.53 vs our +0.16 on same counts.
verification_notes: Corrects earlier local notes: interaction table exists; Ppara n.s. within MD. Xenium slide/mouse mapping UNVERIFIED.

citation: Djouina M et al. 2023. Oral exposure to polyethylene microplastics induces inflammatory and metabolic changes and promotes fibrosis in mouse liver. Ecotoxicol Environ Saf 264:115417
access_level: Full text (publisher PDF); figure images not re-viewed this session; Suppl. Fig. 1 not read
scientific_question: Does dietary PE microbead exposure alter hepatic inflammation, metabolism and fibrosis, alone and on a CCl4 fibrosis background?
design_and_n: Exp 1: CT, 36 um, 116 um, both; n=10/group at 6 wk and 9 wk (separate cohorts). Exp 2: CCl4 +/- beads, n=8/group
exposure_polymer_size_dose_route_duratio: PE beads median 36 um and 116 um, 100 ug/g food per bead type (combined group = 200 ug/g), dietary admixture, 6 or 9 wk; no vehicle or inert-particle control
diet_or_second_factor: Chow; CCl4 as second insult (pairwise only)
statistical_or_ml_models: Mann-Whitney U vs control, p<0.05, no multiple-testing correction; qPCR 2^-ddCt with Polr2a reference
why_model_fits_or_not: Nonparametric two-group tests suit n=10 but ~50 targets x 3 groups x 2 time points without correction inflate false positives; dose and bead combination confounded (combined arm gets double mass)
inputs_features_outputs_targets: Targeted qPCR panel (lipogenesis, FAO, inflammation, fibrosis), liver TG/cholesterol, histology
validation_type: Same-RNA qPCR; Ki-67 IHC; liver biochemistry; no omics, no external data
main_findings: Fasn, Acly, Acaca up in all PE groups at 6 wk (Fasn not significant at 9 wk); Ppara 'two-fold' up per text (earlier figure reading: only combined arm, 116 um arm lower; not re-verified); TG up (combined), cholesterol up (116 um); PE worsened CCl4 fibrosis
actual_limitations: No multiplicity control; no vehicle/inert control; dose-combination confound; primers unpublished; CCl4 frequency inconsistent (Methods twice/wk vs Fig. 7 legend once/wk); authors judge particles unlikely to reach liver
not_attempted_not_a_flaw: Males; transcriptome; metabolic diet; particle biodistribution
relevance_to_our_project: Only independent PE liver gene-level data; our replication found the lipogenic direction OPPOSITE (research/cross_study_replication). Differences: sex, route, diet, platform, timepoint.
verification_notes: Bar-chart fold changes UNVERIFIED this session

citation: Li Q, Zhu K, et al. 2025. Polystyrene microplastics induce liver fibrosis and lipid deposition in mice through three hub genes revealed by the RNA-seq. Sci Rep 15:2583
scientific_question: Which hepatic genes/pathways mediate PS-induced fibrosis and lipid deposition, and does particle size matter?
design_and_n: H2O, 80 nm, 0.5 um, 5 um; 10 allocated/group, 5-8 analysed; RNA-seq n=4/group (16 libraries)
exposure_polymer_size_dose_route_duratio: PS 80 nm, 0.5 um, 5 um, 1 mg/L drinking water, 12 wk; no particle characterisation
statistical_or_ml_models: limma (voom use not stated), |log2FC|>1 & adj p<0.05, 3 pairwise contrasts vs H2O; Venn -> 87 shared DEGs; DAVID enrichment; STRING (>=0.4) + CytoHubba '12 algorithms' -> hub genes; one-way ANOVA + LSD for phenotypes
why_model_fits_or_not: limma-voom valid for n=4, but unclear if applied to counts; hub ranking on a sparse PPI (85 nodes/51 edges) is topology, not evidence of causal relevance; no size-trend model despite ordered sizes; LSD gives no multiplicity control
inputs_features_outputs_targets: Liver counts -> DEGs -> shared DEGs -> PPI hubs; targets fibrosis, inflammation, lipid deposition
validation_type: qPCR n=5-6 (Acot3, Abcc3, Nr1i3 up; Fmo2 failed), likely overlapping mice; histology/IHC/WB for phenotypes; no functional test of hubs, no external data

actual_limitations: Pipeline under-specified; hub genes are predictions; unexplained attrition; LSD; copy errors (oxidative stress 'in ovaries' in males); age discrepancy
not_attempted_not_a_flaw: Females; metabolic diet; dose-response; protein for lipid genes; particle tracking
relevance_to_our_project: Best independent public liver count matrix. Allows same-model re-analysis and size-trend test. Different polymer, strain, route, no vehicle.
verification_notes: Whether qPCR mice overlap sequenced mice UNVERIFIED

citation: Wu D, Smyth GK. 2012. Camera: a competitive gene set test accounting for inter-gene correlation. Nucleic Acids Res 40(17):e133
scientific_question: How to test whether a gene set is more DE than other genes without inflated error from inter-gene correlation?
design_and_n: Simulations and real arrays; residual df 6-27 evaluated (Table 3)
statistical_or_ml_models: Linear-model moderated statistics; variance inflation factor 1+(m-1)rho estimated from residuals
why_model_fits_or_not: Works with any linear-model contrast, including factorial interaction; error control demonstrated at small df (our design has 15 residual df)
inputs_features_outputs_targets: Expression matrix + design + gene sets -> set-level p
how_evaluated: Type I error and power in simulations; real data showing correlation persists in sorted inbred-mouse cells
main_findings: Ignoring correlation inflates competitive-test false positives; camera controls them
actual_limitations: Competitive null asks 'more than other genes', not 'changed at all'; cannot fix confounding in the design
relevance_to_our_project: Already used (supporting); keep for Track A

citation: Wu D, Lim E, Vaillant F, Asselin-Labat ML, Visvader JE, Smyth GK. 2010. ROAST: rotation gene set tests for complex microarray experiments. Bioinformatics 26(17):2176-2182
category: Method: self-contained gene-set test (fry is its fast approximation)
scientific_question: How to test gene sets for any linear-model contrast in small, complex designs while preserving inter-gene correlation?
design_and_n: Simulations incl. 2x2 factorials with 3 or 5 per cell (Section 5.1)
statistical_or_ml_models: Residual rotation (instead of sample permutation) under linear model
why_model_fits_or_not: Closest validated match to our 2x2 n=4-5 design, including interaction contrasts
inputs_features_outputs_targets: Expression + design + contrast + sets -> set-level p (up/down/mixed)
main_findings: Exact-style p-values for small n where permutation has too few distinct permutations
actual_limitations: Self-contained test is sensitive to any global shift, incl. technical (depth) effects aligned with treatment
relevance_to_our_project: Basis of our primary pathway test (fry)

citation: Sweeney TE, Haynes WA, Vallania F, Ioannidis JP, Khatri P. 2017. Methods to increase reproducibility in differential gene expression via meta-analysis. Nucleic Acids Res 45(1):e1
